newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks reach another record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks reach another record close.

text.p: Toronto's key stock index climbed to its 19th record close of the year on Thursday, boosted by a rally in New York and signs that North American central banks have room to hold off hiking interest rates for now.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index rose 39 points to finish at 6588.04, slightly below an intra-day high and new all-time record of 6615.35 points.
Wall Street also rallied, closing up 100 points to 7895.
Market players cheered tame U.S. non-farm payrolls data for June, which showed the economy is growing at a moderate pace, said MMS International analyst Katherine Beattie.

The U.S. Labor Department reported on Thursday that non-farm payrolls rose by 217,000 jobs in June compared to a forecast of 222,000. The U.S. unemployment rate inched up to 5 percent from 4.8 percent after analysts predicted it would remain flat.
"We closed yesterday on a strong note," Beattie said. "We were set for a positive day as long as the U.S. employment report came in as expected or weaker than expected."
Toronto trading was moderate at 90 million shares worth C$1.7 billion ($1.2 billion).
Advancing issues outpaced declining ones 558 to 408 while 276 ended flat.

Only four of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors sagged, led by golds and forestry products. The influential gold group shed almost 2.5 percent and kept Toronto's gains in check after being dragged down by weaker bullion prices. The key Comex price closed $7.10 lower at $325.20.
Interest-sensitive sectors such as banks and utilities extended Wednesday's rally of relief after the U.S. Federal Reserve left short-term interest rates untouched.
A trader added "I don't see any black clouds on the horizon that could hurt the market."
The stronger financial sector included Canada's second largest bank, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, which added 0.70 to 36.55.

Other hot stocks included Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd which hit a new 52-week high of 35 after adding 2.50. The Calgary-based oil firm confirmed that it made a new discovery on its 52-percent owned Masila oil concession in Yemen.
